# Merge simulation results

In practice, results data can be generated by running the `merge_scores()` function, after specifying the desired parameters. This function searches for `.Rdata` files matching a specific naming pattern and merges the extracted scores into a single data frame.

```{r}
# Exemple of merge simulation
p <- 8
d <- 0.4
mp <- 5

results_dir <- here("results")

merged_simus <- merge_scores(results_dir, p = p, d = d, mp = mp)
```


# Plot performances results

## Effect of the distribution settings 

In Figure 1, we fix `p`, `d`, and `mp`, and we plot the effect of the distribution settings on the performance.

```{r}
p <- 12
d <- 0.4
mp <- 5
results_directory <- here("results")

merged_simus <- merge_scores(results_directory, p = p, d = d, mp = mp)

plot_compare_distributions(merged_simus, results_dir = results_directory, save_figure = TRUE)
```

## Effect of the number of nodes

In Figure 2, we fix `d` and `mp`, and we plot the effect of the number of nodes on the performance.

```{r}
d <- 0.4
mp <- 5
results_directory <- here("results")

merged_simus <- merge_scores(results_directory, d = d, mp = mp)

plot_compare_p(merged_simus, results_dir = results_directory, save_figure = TRUE)
```

## Effect of the density

In Figure 3, we fix `p` and `mp`, and we plot the effect of the density on the performance.

```{r}
p <- 16
mp <- 6
results_directory <- here("results")

merged_simus <- merge_scores(results_directory, p = p, mp = mp)

plot_compare_d(merged_simus, results_dir = results_directory, save_figure = TRUE)
```

## Effect of the maximal number of parents

In Figure 4, we fix `p` and `d`, and we plot the effect of the maximal number of parents on the performance.

```{r}
p <- 16
d <- 0.2
results_directory <- here("results")

merged_simus <- merge_scores(results_directory, p = p, d = d)

plot_compare_mp(merged_simus, results_dir = results_directory, save_figure = TRUE)
```

In Figure 5, we show the effect of the maximal number of parents on the computational time.

```{r}
p <- 16
d <- 0.2
results_directory <- here("results")

merged_simus <- merge_scores(results_directory, p = p, d = d)

plot_compare_mp_time(merged_simus, results_dir = results_directory, save_figure = TRUE)
```


## Effect of the Markov blanket size

In Figure 6, we fix `p`, `d`, `mp`, and `nodedists`, and we plot the effect of the Markov blanket size on the performance.

```{r}
p <- 12
d <- 0.4
mp <- 5
nodedists <- "balanced"
results_directory <- here("results")

merged_simus <- merge_mb_scores(results_directory, p = p, d = d, mp = mp, node_dists = "balanced")

plot_compare_mb(merged_simus, results_dir = results_directory, save_figure = TRUE)
```
